item.title: Anthropic Sues Department of Defense Over Supply-Chain-Risk Designation
item.description: The Claude chatbot developer says the Trump administration overstepped by escalating a contract dispute into a federal ban on the company’s technology.

item.title: Feeld Was a Dating App for the Freaks. Now Some People Call It ‘Normie Hell’
item.description: The app that catered to unconventional kinks is gaining steam among daters with vanilla preferences—and some aren’t happy about it.

item.title: Can AI Kill the Venture Capitalist?
item.description: VCs are betting that artificial intelligence will disrupt nearly every industry in the world. Are they prepared for it to disrupt their own?

item.title: This Jammer Wants to Block Always-Listening AI Wearables. It Probably Won’t Work
item.description: Deveillance’s Spectre I, developed by a recent Harvard grad, wants to give people control over the always-on wearables surrounding their lives. The problem? Physics.

item.title: Why Is Alexa+ So Bad?
item.description: I stuck Amazon’s Echo Show 15 and its Alexa+ AI assistant in my kitchen for a month. Things have not gone well.

item.title: Jack Dorsey Is Ready to Explain the Block Layoffs
item.description: In an exclusive interview with WIRED, Block’s cofounder and CEO says he axed 40 percent of his workforce so that he can rebuild the company “as an intelligence.”

item.title: ‘Uncanny Valley’: Iran War in the AI Era, Prediction Market Ethics, and Paramount Beats Netflix
item.description: In this episode, our hosts unpack the ongoing conflict in the Middle East, particularly as the AI industry has been entrenching itself with the Department of Defense.

item.title: OpenAI Had Banned Military Use. The Pentagon Tested Its Models Through Microsoft Anyway
item.description: Sources allege the Defense Department experimented with Microsoft’s version of OpenAI technology before the ChatGPT-maker lifted its prohibition on military applications.

item.title: ByteDance’s AI Ambitions Are Being Hampered by Compute Restraints and Copyright Concerns
item.description: ByteDance’s new Seedance 2.0 AI video model seemed unstoppable—until heavy demand strained the company’s compute capacity and copyright complaints began piling up.

item.title: Grammarly Is Offering ‘Expert’ AI Reviews From Your Favorite Authors—Dead or Alive
item.description: The tool, offered by the recently-rebranded company Superhuman, gives feedback based on the work of famous dead and living writers—without their permission.
